cim: Trump administration rocked by Nvidia shockwave
cim_eredeti: Trump administration rocked by Nvidia shockwave
szoveg_eredeti:
There is no doubt that the November 12 downfall of Nvidia's powerful leader, Jensen Huang, following the revelations of his extramarital affairs, will, one day, be adapted for the screen. For now, this fall, triggered by his partly-acknowledged affairs with a Chinese entrepreneur and two of his subordinates, has destabilized the driving force behind the artificial intelligence revolution, which was running at full speed.

Far from being a mere chip designer, Huang was the mastermind behind a whole business ecosystem, which he fueled with the astronomical profits his company generated. Before the scandals, Nvidia's market capitalization stood at $4 trillion (about €3.63 trillion).

Given the highly centralized corporate structure he had put in place, Huang's departure created a power vacuum that will be difficult to fill. According to The Wall Street Journal, he paid little heed to the person chosen to replace him as interim CEO, Colette Kress, thus highlighting one of the vulnerabilities of the AI sector.

The sector still relies on visionary, larger-than-life business leaders, who often disregard rules they see as intolerable obstacles. For some time, Elon Musk, through his political forays alongside Donald Trump, had embodied the darker side of this new world. Yet this upheaval came from the head of Nvidia, not the boss of SpaceX.

By chance, the shockwave caused by his downfall occurred after the November 3 midterm elections. These elections highlighted a growing sense of unease in American public opinion over these new tech leaders' accelerationist approach. This backlash crystallized around the issue of data centers, energy-hungry facilities that created few jobs. These centers are the backbone of an economy in which startups founded just yesterday are challenging giants like Amazon, Apple, Google, Meta and Microsoft, forcing them into a dizzying race to make investments.

In a country as polarized as the United States, criticism of this phenomenon, which appears to be reckless acceleration, has become a rare point of consensus between Democrats and Republicans. This can be seen in the overwhelming majorities who voted in dozens of local referendums to oppose the creation of new data centers, notably in Ohio.

This climate, which, in its own way, is also fueled by Huang's downfall, will force the AI economy to address questions it has so far brushed aside, whether regarding its final purpose or its sustainability.

In the short term, Trump's administration must now explain the considerable leeway Nvidia's leader enjoyed in exporting his products, to the point where he seemed able to influence decisions about US relations with Beijing. Tensions have already emerged between two major figures in the US president's team, Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent and Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, over a possible circumvention restrictions on exporting Nvidia's most advanced chips to China. These all signal major turbulence ahead.
